newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Aussie sellers set course for 73 cents.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Aussie sellers set course for 73 cents.

text.p: *AUD testing sub-74 cent levels for first time since January 1996 following a panic retreat from $0.7440 in face of US sales
*Pullback ruined a fledgling rally and reaffirmed force of downtrend with analysts tipping 1996 low of 73 cents medium term
*Metals prices steadied, but CRB also in downtrend. Risk of rate cut dominates but lack of data suggests not this week
By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the local currency was teetering at US$0.7396/01 having fled all the way from US$0.7445/50 late here on Friday.
This was its lowest start since January last year when the dollar had just troughed at US$0.7305 and was embarking on a year long uptrend which saw it peak at 82 cents last December.

Since then support had been sapped by two cuts in domestic interest rates which took money rates here below those in the U.S. for the first time in most dealers' memory. Another 0.5 point easing in the 5.50 percent cash rate was already priced and the only doubt in the market's mind concerned timing.
Analysts reckoned a dearth of domestic data this week meant there was nothing for the RBA to link a move to and expected it to wait for Q2 consumer price and wages figures on July 23/24.
If these showed inflation was as benign as expected, then most felt a cut would be a better than 50/50 chance, perhaps immediately or maybe after the RBA board meeting on August 5.

Partial data on inflation this week would offer a hint on how pressures were faring and, in particular, if the fall in the dollar was impacting inflation. Manufacturing output prices for May, due today, and input prices, out Tuesday, have been very weak with falls of 0.2 and 0.5 percent respectively in April.

Typically changes in the currency take some months to feed through and, in any case, analysts are uncertain how much scope manufacturers have to raise their prices given the subdued state of domestic demand.

The lack of inflationary pressure was not confined to Australia and, indeed, has contributed to the A$'s troubles by keeping commodity prices subdued despite rising world growth. Thus the Commodity Research Bureau index did steady somewhat Friday, but remains close to two-year lows.
On the crosses the yen surged this morning pushing the A$ down to 83.96/06 from 84.67/77. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
